data.title: S&P 500 Dividend Yield Hits Historic Lows: 5 Dividend ETFs to Consider — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Teresa Rivas

From the pandemic era of ultra-low interest rates to today's paltry payout from major companies, it feels like income-focused investors can't catch a break. For those unwilling to move entirely into bonds, it's time to think outside the box — or in this case, the index.

At present, the S&P 500's dividend yield is 1.04%, which is "effectively its lowest level...in history (including back-testing)," Sevens Report President Tom Essaye wrote Friday. That record surpasses even the 1.09% it had fallen to during the peak of the dot-com bubble of the late 1990s and early 2000s, when tech companies' hyper-growth hype dominated the index and dividends were viewed as stodgy and out of fashion.

Of course, the S&P 500 is partly a victim of its own success. It's climbed more than 13% since the start of the year and recorded 28 new all-time closing highs in 2026. When prices go up, yields go down.

However, that's cold comfort to seniors and other investors who depend on dividends — and for many years were right to do so.

Historically, the S&P 500 has sported an average dividend yield of 4.2%, Essaye notes, and it's not just seniors who should be concerned about the decline, given that over time, "dividends have materially contributed to an investor's total return" in the past. He cites data from Hartford Funds, which found reinvested dividends and the power of compounding accounted for 85% of the S&P 500's cumulative total return since 1960.

Translated into dollars, that means $10,000 invested in the S&P 500 in 1960 would have grown by 2025 to roughly $1.14 million without dividends, or $7.58 million with dividends reinvested. So the gains from dividends aren't small potatoes.

Still, investors don't have to give up hope entirely, even when excluding super-high-yielding exchange-traded funds (possible "yield traps") and dividend growth ETFs, which tend to have yields not much higher than the index.

Essaye highlights the SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 High Dividend ETF, the iShares Select Dividend ETF, the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF and outside U.S. equities, the iShares International Select Dividend ETF, and iShares Emerging Markets Dividend ETF. All five yield at least three times as much as the S&P 500's current level and use leverage or derivatives either minimally or not at all.

That may not be as easy as buying and holding the index, but investors ignore the power of dividends at their own peril.

data.title: Trump Announces White House Hearing to Investigate Fed's Lisa Cook — WSJ
data.description:
By Matt Grossman and Brian Schwartz

President Trump has formed a committee to evaluate the mortgage-fraud allegations against Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook and has scheduled an in-person hearing at the White House for Nov. 5.

Trump said Cook would "be examined" by the committee, which would then recommend whether to remove her from the Fed, according to a memo posted on the White House's website.

The announcement marks a dramatic escalation in the president's long-running attempt to wield more control over the Fed and could deliver the unusual spectacle of a central-bank official arriving at the White House for a disciplinary meeting.

The central bank is set up to operate independently from the White House, an arrangement seen by economists as essential for allowing it to set interest rates without political considerations.

Trump tried to fire Cook last year, but the Supreme Court ruled this summer that she hadn't been given sufficient opportunity to present her case.

The Trump memo lays out a step-by-step process that seems designed to respond to the court's ruling. It maps out logistical details such as when Cook may submit her own "position statement" and how long the hearing can last ("no longer than 4 hours").

The White House committee will include Kevin Hassett, the assistant to the president for economic policy. It will also include the chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and the director of the Office of Government Ethics. EEOC Chair Andrea Lucas and the OGE's current acting director, Keith Sonderling, who also serves as labor secretary, were both appointed by Trump.

"Governor Cook shall appear at the hearing and be examined by the Committee, its representatives, and her legal counsel, if any," said a presidential memorandum dated Oct. 7. "The Committee shall submit written findings of fact and conclusions of law to me and shall recommend whether there is cause to remove Governor Cook from her position."

The memo said that the hearing would be closed to the public but would be transcribed.

The Cook case marks the first-ever attempted presidential firing of a sitting Fed governor.

In a statement, two lawyers for Cook, Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen, said that they have contacted the White House to "evaluate whether the process proposed has a possibility of being a genuine one and not simply a box checking exercise."

"In light of the President's repeated statements that he has already decided to fire Governor Cook — regardless of the facts and evidence — we have grave doubts that this 'hearing' is a legitimate one that would conform to the law," the lawyers said. "But if it is anything close to objective, the conclusion will be that Governor Cook did not commit mortgage fraud, leaving no cause to remove her."

The hearing would refocus attention on core questions of the Fed's independence and Trump's attempts to gain more control over how the central bank sets interest rates. Trump has long complained that rates are too high and has taken unprecedented steps to pressure the Fed, including a criminal investigation of Jerome Powell, the former chair.

In Trump's telling, the chairman he chose to succeed Powell, Kevin Warsh, has been prevented from cutting rates by a "very political" Fed board. Fed policymakers including Warsh voted unanimously to raise interest rates last month.

Cook was appointed to the Fed's board by former President Joe Biden and is serving a term that runs until 2038.

Last year, Trump adviser Bill Pulte, the head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, produced documents that he said showed Cook had listed more than one property as her "primary residence" on mortgage paperwork. Trump seized on the discrepancy and attempted to fire Cook over the alleged misconduct, a decision he announced abruptly on social media.

She sued to block her firing and has said she never committed mortgage fraud. The laws establishing the Fed say that top officials can be fired only "for cause," a legal term whose application to Fed officials had never been directly tested.

Earlier this year, the Supreme Court largely sided with Cook, ruling that she couldn't be fired without some minimal procedural protections that would allow the evidence to be aired. The ruling returned the litigation to federal district court, where Cook's original lawsuit is pending.

Since the Supreme Court ruling, the president and some of his allies have continued to look for ways to potentially oust Cook from the board. This summer, a Trump aide sent Cook a letter outlining the mortgage-fraud allegations and asking her to respond. That appeared to be an attempt to follow the process requirements that the Supreme Court outlined.

Write to Matt Grossman at matt.grossman@wsj.com and Brian Schwartz at brian.schwartz@wsj.com

data.title: Palantir Stock Jumps as Barclays Turns Bullish on Software Giant
data.description:
Palantir Technologies (PLTR) shares gained 2.5% on Friday morning after Barclays began covering the software company with an Overweight rating and a $265 price target, signaling confidence in its growth prospects and profitability.

Barclays analyst Anthony Valentini pointed to Palantir's competitive advantages as a key factor behind the rating. The company develops software that helps businesses and government agencies analyze data and make operational decisions.

The new target suggests further upside from Palantir's recent trading level. The rating also adds to Wall Street's assessment of the company as investors weigh its growth potential against its valuation.

Palantir has drawn attention for its artificial intelligence software and its work with commercial and government customers. Its ability to maintain customer demand and convert revenue growth into profits will remain important as investors assess whether the stock can justify its market valuation.

The latest analyst coverage comes as investors continue to evaluate opportunities in AI-related software companies. Barclays' rating gives Palantir another positive Wall Street assessment, although the stock's future performance will depend on business execution and financial results.

data.title: Strategy, Robinhood and Coinbase Jump as Trump Eases Iran Attack Fears
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) recovered on Friday as President Donald Trump's comments eased concerns about a possible U.S. attack on Iran before the November midterm elections. The rebound offered some relief to cryptocurrency investors after a week of losses.

Strategy (MSTR) climbed 2.5% in morning trading. Robinhood Markets (HOOD) advanced 1.5%, while Coinbase Global (COIN) gained 1.9%.

Despite the recovery, Bitcoin remained down 2.2% for the week, putting the cryptocurrency on track for its steepest weekly decline since September. The pullback reflects lingering uncertainty as investors weigh geopolitical tensions, energy prices and broader market conditions.

Analyst price-target increases also offered support for crypto-related shares. Barclays raised its target for Strategy to $175 from $160, while Morgan Stanley lifted its targets for Robinhood to $160 from $150 and Coinbase to $258 from $250.

Brent crude oil fell about 1.5% to roughly $103 a barrel as markets assessed the potential implications of Trump's remarks for regional tensions and energy supplies. Whether Friday's rebound can continue may depend on geopolitical developments and the direction of cryptocurrency prices.

data.title: Samsung Stocks Hold Flat After Profit Vaults Nearly Ninefold
data.description:
Samsung Electronics (SSNLF), the memory and consumer-electronics manufacturer, estimated third-quarter operating profit of ?107.4 trillion on sales of ?195 trillion, while its shares closed at ?262,000, down 2.42% in Seoul on October 8. Huge earnings. A falling stock. Investors still need a reason to believe this profit surge can last.

According to Yonhap, the preliminary operating-profit estimate represents a 782.5% jump from a year earlier. Samsung's projected figures imply a companywide operating margin of roughly 55.1%more than half of revenue flowing into operating profit. The GF Score graphic shows 92 out of 100, with strong profitability, growth, financial strength and momentum, but a much weaker GF Value reading that makes valuation the obvious pressure point.

The next test comes on October 29, when Reuters reports Samsung will publish detailed results and divisional earnings. Investors need the breakdown: how much profit reflects durable AI-memory demand, how much reflects pricing, and whether premium memory is strengthening Samsung's competitive position. The headline numbers show earnings power. The details must show staying power.

data.title: SAP Stocks Gain as TechWolf Adds Workforce Intelligence
data.description:
SAP , the enterprise-software and business-AI provider, agreed to buy TechWolf, adding workforce intelligence to its AI push, while U.S. shares traded at $213.99, up roughly 0.75% at 11.15 EST on Friday, October 9. The opportunity is straightforward: help employers identify the skills they already have and the gaps they need to fill. The valuation snapshot puts shares 16.23% below the $255.45 GF Value estimate, suggesting potential upside without guaranteeing a bargain.

According to SAP's announcement, TechWolf draws on existing HR and business systems to connect employee skills, everyday tasks and labor-market information. SAP plans to embed that intelligence deeper into SuccessFactors, giving hiring, training and workforce planning better foundations. TechWolf's platform is expected to remain available to customers outside SAP's ecosystem. Closing is targeted for the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approval and other customary conditions. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Better workforce data could give SAP's AI tools more useful answersand give customers another reason to buy. But a stronger product does not automatically mean stronger earnings. SAP still needs to turn that intelligence into paid adoption while keeping integration manageable and sensitive employee information protected. With the purchase price undisclosed and future sales gains unproven, the deal makes SAP's AI strategy more concrete. Its financial payoff still needs to show up.

data.title: ATEX, NN, GOGO Stocks Gain: SpaceX’s $8B Spectrum Deal Could Boost Low-Band Spectrum Value, Says Roth Capital
data.description:
Key points:
  • Roth estimates that applying SpaceX’s reported price per MHZ would value Gogo’s spectrum holdings at about $2.3 billion.
  • The firm sees potential benefits for Aviat Networks and Ceragon Networks, which provide wireless networking and communications equipment.
  • Roth believes the SpaceX deal could potentially strengthen AST SpaceMobile’s relationships with major U.S. telecom operators.

Anterix (ATEX), NextNav (NN) and Gogo (GOGO) could benefit from rising demand for wireless spectrum following SpaceX’s (SPCX) reported $8 billion acquisition of Grain Management’s low-band frequencies, according to Roth Capital.

The firm believes the acquisition could increase the value of low-band spectrum controlled by the three companies. Roth estimates that applying SpaceX’s reported price per megahertz would value Gogo’s spectrum holdings alone at about $2.3 billion, compared with its roughly $1 billion enterprise value.

Anterix holds nationwide spectrum licenses in the 900 MHz band, primarily used for wireless networks for utilities, while NextNav controls lower 900 MHz spectrum used for positioning, navigation and timing services.

At the time of writing, ATEX shares were up over 10%, NN stock gained 6%, and GOGO edged up 2.7%.

AVNW, CRNT Could Benefit Says Roth

Roth also sees potential benefits for Aviat Networks (AVNW) and Ceragon Networks (CRNT), which provide wireless networking and communications equipment. Both companies could see increased demand as SpaceX builds out its ground-based mobile network and traditional telecom operators invest in infrastructure to compete with Starlink.

AVNW and CRNT shares were up around 1.6% each.

Roth Believes SPCX Deal Could Push ASTS Closer To Telecom Operators

The firm said the deal could also reshape competition in satellite communications, potentially strengthening AST SpaceMobile’s (ASTS) relationships with major U.S. telecom operators.

It expects AST SpaceMobile to emerge as a preferred independent satellite-to-phone connectivity partner for these carriers.

Berenberg echoed the bullish thesis, adding that AST SpaceMobile is the only satellite-to-phone company that can provide broadband connectivity to existing mobile devices while working directly with telecom operators.

However, ASTS was down nearly 15%, its sharpest single-day losses since mid-July.

T, VZ, TMUS Stocks Decline

On Thursday, SpaceX announced plans to acquire up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band from Grain Management. These low-frequency airwaves can travel long distances and penetrate buildings.

The deal, which remains subject to regulatory approval, is expected to increase competition for AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile (TMUS), whose stocks fell 9% to 13%.

Retail’s Take On ATEX, NN, GOGO

Retail sentiment surrounding NN was ‘extremely bullish’ on Stocktwits, while sentiment for ATEX and GOGO trended in the ‘bullish’ territory.

ATEX shares have surged 278%, significantly outperforming NN and GOGO, whose shares are down about 25% and 51%, respectively.

data.title: Nigerian Payments Company OPay Files for IPO
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Payments company OPay filed for an initial public offering of American depositary shares.

The company plans to trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker OPAY. It didn't disclose the amount or pricing of the ADSs it plans to offer.

OPay, which facilitates digital payments and loans, launched in Nigeria in 2018 and continues to do the majority of its business there. It has other operations in Indonesia, Egypt and Pakistan.

The company aims to expand across more African countries with a focus on offering financial infrastructure in emerging markets that have limited traditional banking systems.

Loan financing made up about half of sales in 2025, with transaction-based services and loan-facilitation services making up the other half.

Revenue from Nigeria made up 88% of total sales in 2025. Total sales roughly doubled, to $536.3 million.

data.title: Lumentum Can't Keep Up With AI Demand-and Its Stock Is Surging — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mariapaula Gonzalez

Shares of Lumentum and other optical networking stocks, advanced Friday after CEO Michael Hurlston said the company has almost sold out of its optical parts through 2029 and will struggle to keep up with demand in the near future.

In an interview with Bloomberg TV on Friday, Hurlston said the company has almost sold out of its optoelectronic parts through 2029 and has struggled to meet demand for its laser chips.

"We are really trying to catch up, add capacity as fast as we can, but we are very, very far behind where customers want," Hurlston said.

He explained that Lumentum won't be able to meet 30% of demand for some products through 2028, with other items facing an even steeper 70% shortfall through next year.

Lumentum didn't respond to a request from Barron's to confirm the information.

That "sold out" notice offered further evidence of strong demand for artificial-intelligence hardware, as optical networking stocks rose Friday. Lumentum stock rose 7.4% to $1,125.25. Meanwhile, Coherent and Applied Optoelectronics gained 2.3% and 5.7%, respectively.

Lumentum's supply shortfall could mean that hyperscalers, such as Microsoft, will turn to other optical suppliers, such as Coherent and Applied Optoelectronics, to fill the gap.

Lumentum supplies advanced indium phosphide devices that support high-speed computing and data flow. Hurlston said shipments for Lumentum's laser chips, which are essentially small engines that translate electricity into light, have fallen "vastly behind" demand.

With demand outstripping supply, component makers could have room to raise prices and improve profit margins.

Having production capacity fully committed through 2029 also gives suppliers and investors some visibility into future revenue. It could also ease concerns that the AI infrastructure spending boom will prove short-lived.

Optical component stocks have become huge winners from the AI infrastructure boom that began this year, as spending on data centers and high-speed networking has surged. For instance, earlier this year, Nvidia announced investments of $2 billion each in Lumentum and Coherent.

data.title: Netflix Is Reportedly Preparing to Lay Off 5% Of Workforce Amid Growth Slowdown
data.description:
Key points:
  • Netflix plans to cut about 5% of its workforce as early as next week, potentially affecting hundreds of roles across its 16,000 full-time staff worldwide. 
  • The company’s stock has plummeted roughly 42% since initiating a bid for Warner Bros. Discovery Inc.
  • Netflix is expanding into live broadcasts, podcasts, gaming, and international partnerships to reignite viewer engagement. 

Netflix Inc. (NFLX) is preparing to lay off about 5% of its global workforce as early as next week, according to a report by media newsletter Puck.

A representative for the streaming giant declined to comment on the reported job reductions.

Based on regulatory filings from late last year, Netflix employed roughly 16,000 full-time staff members, with approximately 68% located in the United States. A 5% reduction would affect around 800 employees across the organization.

Investor Skepticism

The reported restructuring follows months of pressure on the company's valuation. Netflix shares have fallen about 42% since the service pursued an acquisition of rival media titan Warner Bros. Discovery Inc.(WBD) last year.

Wall Street saw the buyout effort as a rare departure for a firm that has historically grown through organic expansion rather than major corporate consolidation.

The bid ultimately ended after Warner Bros. was acquired by the newly rebranded Skydance Corp.

Slowing Revenue and Engagement Challenges

Beyond market turbulence, Netflix faces operational pressures around viewer retention and content reception. Platform engagement grew by just 2% in the most recent reporting period, while its Emmy Awards haul fell to a decade low.

In recent years, the company implemented several monetization strategies, including launching a subscription tier with advertisements, curbing password sharing, and raising subscription prices. Despite these efforts, top-line sales growth has continued to cool.

At the Bloomberg Screen Time conference in Los Angeles, Co-Chief Executive Officer Ted Sarandos acknowledged the slowdown, admitting the platform's current trajectory is behind executive expectations.

Diversifying Content Operations

To reignite platform engagement, Netflix has been expanding beyond traditional film and television programming. The streaming platform has increasingly invested in live event broadcasting, video gaming offerings, and podcasts, while also licensing third-party catalog content, including an agreement with French broadcaster TF1.

Financial analysts and investors will closely monitor the company's performance when Netflix reports its upcoming quarterly results on Oct. 20.

NFLX Stock: Retail View 

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bullish’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

NFLX stock has lost about 25% year-to-date.

data.title: Hedge funds cut Bitcoin, brokerages load up in Q2: CoinShares report
data.description:
Professional investors increased their Bitcoin holdings in second-quarter, even as overall U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF holdings declined, according to a CoinShares report published Friday.

13F filers held 264K BTC at the end of June, up 1.3% from 261K tokens in the first-quarter. Meanwhile, total U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF holdings fell 6.3%, and non-13F holders reduced their exposure by 8.3%.

The dollar value of 13F filers’ holdings fell 13% to $15.5B as Bitcoin’s price declined 14% during the quarter. However, their share of total U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF AUM rose to 22.4% from 20.8%, marking the first increase since second-quarter 2025.

Hedge funds cut exposure as brokerages buy

Hedge funds recorded the largest reduction, cutting their Bitcoin exposure by 10.8K coins (22%) to 37.8K BTC.

DE Shaw exited its 3.7K BTC position, while Millennium Management reduced its holdings from 14.4K BTC to 7.3K BTC.

Investment advisors also trimmed exposure, reducing holdings by 4.6K BTC, or 3%, to 145.7K BTC. Brevan Howard cut its position by 9.6K BTC to 4.1K BTC.

The advisors nevertheless accounted for roughly 55% of all reported 13F Bitcoin holdings.

At the same time, brokerage holdings more than doubled to 38.5K BTC from 17K BTC. Jane Street added 10.9K BTC to reach 16.9K BTC, while Morgan Stanley held 10.4K BTC. However, Morgan Stanley’s Q1 filing was excluded from the earlier comparison, partly affecting the increase.

Bank of Montreal and VanEck Associates each added roughly 2.6K BTC.

Other notable sellers included Avenir Tech, which reduced its position by 2.8K BTC, SIG Holding, which cut 2.4K BTC, and IMC-Chicago, which reduced its holdings by 2.3K BTC.

Government and university endowment holdings remained broadly unchanged, while private-equity exposure rose 5% to 6.9K BTC.

Now, the third-quarter filings will show whether brokerage buying continues and whether professional investors maintain their Bitcoin exposure following the second-quarter decline.

data.title: Businesses add 193,000 Bitcoin in 2026 while individuals sell 93,000
data.description:
Companies are still buying Bitcoin in 2026. Most of them just aren't the ones doing it.

Businesses have added 193,000 BTC so far this year, according to a River Financial report published on October 8, 2026. Over the same stretch, individuals were net sellers of 93,000 BTC.

River's figures put total corporate Bitcoin holdings at 1.64 million BTC. That equals 7.8% of the total Bitcoin supply.

This is the second straight year businesses have been the largest net buyers of Bitcoin, per the report.

Year-to-date business inflows came to $15.7 billion. River's data shows that is down approximately two-thirds from where things stood at this point in 2025.

The concentration is the real story. Strategy and Strive together added 197,000 BTC, which River says accounts for more than 100% of net business purchases. Strategy alone now holds 848,000 BTC.

Every other Bitcoin treasury company combined contributed just 8,000 BTC.

Bitcoin miners are on the opposite side of the trade. River's report shows miners net sold 32,800 BTC this year.

According to the report, miners sold to fund spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Individuals have had a more complicated year. River's data shows they were net sellers of approximately 140,000 BTC in the first half of 2026. Then the direction changed.

In the third quarter, individuals flipped to net accumulation of 107,000 BTC. Even with that rebound, the year-to-date total still shows individuals as net sellers of 93,000 BTC.

River ties the slowdown to fading momentum in Bitcoin treasury strategies after the 2025 crypto bull market. The 2026 numbers show what happens after the party. River's framing points to reduced demand for the treasury model itself, not just a pause in purchasing.

For anyone watching Bitcoin's supply and demand, the headline business number can be misleading. A 193,000 BTC net purchase reads like broad institutional adoption. In practice, it reflects the conviction of two companies, offset by net selling from the rest of the corporate field.

The report also suggests corporations may adopt more conservative treasury strategies going forward.

The miner data adds another wrinkle. Selling to fund AI infrastructure means a portion of new Bitcoin supply is being converted into capital for a separate industry. If that shift continues, miner selling may become tied to AI spending cycles rather than just Bitcoin's own economics.

Their Q3 swing to net buying of 107,000 BTC is the most notable change in direction in the report.

data.title: U.S. Oil Rig Count Rises By 6 to 462 — Market Talk

data.title: Microsoft is nearing a big milestone that solidifies its revival
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

Microsoft is close to reclaiming a $4 trillion market cap - and fresh records are also in sight

Microsoft is nearing a $4 trillion market cap for the first time since last October.

Microsoft is closing in on $4 trillion territory for the first time in nearly a year, helping to cap a wild ride that's seen the company find its way back into investors' good graces.

Worth $3.97 trillion as of midday Friday, Microsoft (MSFT) is not only on the verge of recapturing a $4 trillion market capitalization but it is also within a hair of its highest-ever market value. Microsoft was last worth $4 trillion on Oct. 29, 2025, and it hit a peak market cap of $4.029 trillion the day before that, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Microsoft is the fourth-largest company in the U.S., behind Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL) and Amazon.com (AMZN).

The round trip since last October encapsulates how Microsoft first fell out of fashion on Wall Street in the face of concerns about its cloud growth and the durability of its software business. Lately, however, investors are seeing those businesses in a fresh light, and Microsoft has re-emerged as a stable software bet at a time when investors are questioning how turbulence at top AI labs could impact the companies that rely on their models and spending.

Shares of Microsoft are up more than 50% from their 2026 low, logged in June.

Microsoft has carved out a niche as a model-agnostic software company, meaning its software offerings aren't tied to one model. It's also sporting a growth story that stands out on Wall Street.

D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch that the acceleration is a big reason for investors' renewed optimism. The company has seen increasing returns on its AI spending, he said.

As long as Microsoft continues to demonstrate healthy cloud growth, AI returns and adoption of its Copilot assistant, the company is likely to continue on its growth trajectory, StoneX analyst Yi Fu Lee told MarketWatch.

Lee added that Microsoft's hardware event earlier this week, which featured an appearance by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to help show off an AI laptop collaboration, is a prime example of how Microsoft is broadening its AI strategy. At the event, Microsoft touted its Surface laptop, which runs on Nvidia systems and shows how the company is seeking to capitalize on AI beyond just software and the cloud.

More from MarketWatch: Microsoft and Nvidia are teaming up on a supercharged AI laptop

More broadly, investors view the legacy software giant as trustworthy, Argus Research analyst Joseph Bonner told MarketWatch last week.

He said that "corporate America may just have more trust" in Azure and Microsoft's AI harnesses - or the software that enables a large language model to execute tasks and run tools - more "than any of the frontier AI labs."

Shares of Microsoft were up roughly 2% in afternoon action on Friday.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: US Gulf producers shut in more oil and gas as Isaias nears landfall
data.description:
Key points:
  • Shut-ins equal nearly 72% of Gulf oil output and 59% of natural gas, agency says
  • Crews evacuate 129 staffed production platforms, or 35% of Gulf total, agency says
  • Earth Science Associates says hurricane could disrupt roughly 7.2 million barrels of Gulf oil production

US producers in the Gulf of Mexico shut in about 1.5 million barrels per day of oil production and 1.3 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas, an increase from Thursday, as Hurricane Isaias churned toward the coast ahead of an expected landfall along the Florida Panhandle late on Friday.

The shut-ins represent nearly 72% and 59% of US oil and natural gas production in the Gulf, respectively, according to the Marine Minerals Administration.

Personnel have been evacuated from 129 production platforms, representing 35% of the 371 staffed platforms in the Gulf of Mexico, the agency said. It added that crews had also been evacuated from eight non-dynamically positioned rigs.

The US federal offshore Gulf of Mexico produces about 2 million barrels of oil a day, according to the US Energy Information Administration, or roughly 15% of total US crude output. The region also produces an average of about 2.1 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas.

Isaias, the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, has strengthened into a Category 3 hurricane and is moving north-northeast. Weakening is expected after the storm makes landfall, according to the National Hurricane Center.

The hurricane could disrupt roughly 7.2 million barrels of Gulf oil production, according to Earth Science Associates. The consulting firm cut its forecast from 9 million barrels on Thursday as the storm's projected path tracked eastward.

The companies with the most exposure to the storm include BP , Chevron , ENI , Murphy Oil and Shell , among others, according to the Earth Science model.

Shell said late on Thursday it had completed evacuations at its Appomattox, Mars, Ursa, Olympus and Vito facilities, while production remained shut in at Mars, Ursa, Olympus and Vito.

Chevron has evacuated most personnel from its Gulf of Mexico facilities, while maintaining production at four operated platforms and shutting in output at the remaining five.

"At our onshore facilities, we continue to follow our established storm preparedness procedures and are closely monitoring the projected path of the hurricane," the company said in a statement on Friday.

About 500,000 barrels of daily refining capacity are in the storm’s path, including the Pascagoula, Mississippi, refinery, Energy Aspects estimated.
